It reveals from the case record that vide order dated 2nd May, 2025, this Court passed the following order:
" This matter is taken up through Hybrid arrangement (video conferencing/physical mode).

This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner Manas Ranjan Pradhan challenging the order dated 17.04.2024 under Annexure-1 dated 16.04.2024 passed by the General Manager, Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd., Lakhanpur Area, opposite party no.4.

It appears that the petitioner earlier approached this Court in W.P.(C) No. 36066 of 2023, which was disposed of on 27.02.2024 and the opposite party no.4 was asked to consider and dispose of the representation filed by the petitioner and to pass appropriate order within a period of three months from the Designation: JUNIOR STENOGRAPHER Location: HIGH COURT OF ORISSA, CUTTACK Date:
11-Jul-2025 11:52:47 date of production of certified copy of the order.
Learned counsel for the petitioner files the copy of the order dated 27.02.2024, which is taken on record.

On perusal of the impugned order, it appears that opposite party no.4 found that the petitioner Intentionally/knowingly purchased the land after 11(1) notification under CBA (A & D) Act, 1957 to get compensation and R & R benefits and therefore, it was observed that his case has no merit.
From the said order, it reveals that 11(1) notification was issued on 15.12.1988.

When we made a query to the learned counsel for the petitioner as to when the petitioner purchased the land, learned counsel for the petitioner seeks some time to produce the relevant documents in that respect on the next date.

List this matter in the week commencing from 30th June 2025."
5.
The matter was then listed on 2nd July, 2025, when learned counsel for the Petitioner sought for an adjournment.

While granting adjournment to learned counsel for the Petitioner, this Court was made it clear that no further prayer for adjournment at the instance of the Petitioner shall be entertained on the next date, i.e., today.
6. Since none appears for the Petitioner to pursue the matter, this Court has no other option other than to dismiss the writ petition.
7. Accordingly, this writ petition is dismissed for non- prosecution.
(K.R. Mohapatra)
